main_text.p: tum exteriorem. Et probatur, nam quo magis descendunt lineæ ab externo circulo, magis accedunt inter se, vnde maiora semper designabunt, seu relinquent spatia in primo circulo, & minora in secundo. Quare ad hoc tandem erit deueniendum, vt occupparo circulo toto concentrico, adhuc maneant spatia in externo ad linearum ductiones, vt patet in hac figura.

Hoc autem dato, non possunt â quouis puncto loculorum a.b. c. d. cæterisque in peripheria manentibus duci lineæ ad centrum, eò quòd aliquando tandem non aderunt in circulo minori spatia vlla, per quæ transeant sine penetratione, vt patet in superiori parte lineis occupata. Vnde patet non verificari axioma, quòd ab omni puncto ad omne duci possit linea (nisi mentaliter, & in abstracto) constat igitur, pauciora esse puncta in minori circulo, quàm in maiori: ab isto enim aliæ possent deduci lineæ, quæ non transirent per illum.

page.notes: The diagram (a circle with radiating lines and sectors lettered A, B, C, D) is described, not transcribed. The word "occupparo" and "vt patet in" with the line-end mark are printed as seen. The last line "ni" is a catchword-like fragment at the foot of the column, kept in the text. Faint marks at the bottom right are a digitiser's stamp and were left out.
